question.text: SEBI introduced 'Accredited Investors' to provide flexibility on minimums and certain compliance. Which of the following is TRUE about Accredited Investors under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Accredited Investors must be a subset of retail investors to qualify
Accredited Investors (AIs) may avail flexibility in minimum investment amount and are excluded from the 1,000 investor count
Accredited Investors are prohibited from investing in any AIF
Accredited Investor status is granted by the Ministry of Finance, not SEBI

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 7: AIs are HNIs/institutions meeting a net-worth/income threshold; they can avail relaxed minimums (e.g., AI-only funds, Large Value Funds for AIs) and are excluded from the 1,000 investor count — giving Managers additional scheme-capacity runway. **The Trap:** Option A reverses the concept. Option C is false. Option D misallocates authority — it is a SEBI regime. **Cross-Exam Context:** Accredited Investor framework is a recent addition (2021); XIX-C tests it in detail. XIX-A/B reference it briefly. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For Large Value Funds for AIs, minimum ticket is INR 70 crore per AI — a different universe. Keep AI-only documentation ready so you can pivot to an AI-only scheme if a whale LP demands bespoke terms.
